There are three skill levels. The easiest one has only two operators: +1 and +10. The two later levels have both additions and multiplications. Level 2 has always the same addition operation (+10) while on level 3 it is randomly selected from between two and nine. The multiplication operation is random on both levels from between two and five. Additionally there is an option for night driving. It differs in that the equations are not spelled out meaning that the player has to keep track of the mileage in his head.

199477.overview:
MasterType is an educational game that teaches the player how to type with the keyboard. In the game the MasterType is a powerful wizard who is helping the player defending his command ship by using his laser like force. The command ship is stationed in the center of the screen and from each corner of the screen missiles are launched toward the ship. In each corner of the screen there is a word and by successfully typing in these words the wizard uses his force to zap the missiles. The command ship has four areas and when an area has been hit by a missile it's shield will be destroyed. If the same area is hit a second time the whole ship will explode and the game will be over.

The game consists of 17 or 18 lessons depending on version and is chosen before the game begins. The first lesson deals with the home row keys (a to ;) and the player only has to enter single letters. As the difficulty increases with each lesson longer and more complex phrases needs to be typed in. Once a lesson is completed the player gets a summary showing how well he has done and whether further practice is needed. Some options exist to alter the game after the player's needs. A beginner mode can be turned on and it's also possible to set a speed goal (number of words per minute). In addition to the lessons included, it is also possible for the player to create his own lessons.

199716.overview:
Musical Pilot is a 1-player arcade game for the 8-bit Atari computer.

The player controls a small airplane which can fly up and down on a musical scale. As the player flies, balloons which correspond to musical notes appear on the screen, and the appropriate note is played. The player tries to hit the balloon with their propeller. If the player strikes all balloons in a song, they advance to a more difficult stage. There is 4 stages in all, and the player gets a total of 4 chances to try to reach and complete the final stage. The player receives 1 point for each balloon destroyed. If a balloon is missed, the player must repeat that level, and can not advance to the highest rank.

199823.overview:
Space journey is an educational math game for multiple systems.

The player controls a spaceship, and must answer math questions in order to perform actions with their vessel. The player has 2 minutes to guide their spaceship back to Earth. The player must answer mathematical questions to move their spaceship, and they must intercept 10 meteors or land on 5 planets before returning to the Earth. The player will be lost in space permanently if they strike a meteor or do not return to the Earth within 2 minutes. Along the way, the player encounters dangers including force fields, meteor showers, refueling stations, and others which require answering math questions to escape. There are 3 levels of difficulty.

199826.overview:
Mogul Maniac is a 1st-person perspective (although you can see your ski's) skiing game where the objective is to get through the open and and closed gates as quickly as possible.

The gates consists of 2 poles of the same color: either red or blue of which the objective is to ski between those poles.

The game consists of 9 different courses as well as 2 different difficulty settings (novice and expert). In the novice setting you will be penalized 5 seconds for each gate you miss, the expert setting however automatically disqualifies you if you miss a gate (although you still can complete the run).

There also is no limit to the number of players that can play, but only the fastest time will be shown on the screen.

200738.overview:
Meteor is a simple game of dodging a screen-covering meteor shower that moves from right to left on your screen. You can maneuver your ship in any direction with the stick as you attempt to dodge the oncoming swarm.

Because of how dense the playfield is, Meteor feels more like a racing game than a space one, with you constantly dodging to find lanes among the rocks.

200741.overview:
The game reenacts the events between June 4 and June 7, 1942 during the Battle of Midway, which was the turning point for Allied Forces in the Pacific Theater. Gameplay is turn based with each turn representing one hour of the battle. The player controls Task force 16, comprising the Enterprise and Hornet aircraft carriers, Task force 17 comprising Yorktown, and Midway Island. Each task force may be moved on a map in any direction by providing a direction in degrees. During each turn Consolidated PBY Catalinas scout out the location of the enemy Task force comprising Akagi, Kaga, Soryu, Hiryu, and Zuiho.

Once a Task Force has been identified and are within range a strike group may be launched from neighboring ships. Planes are generally in three conditions throughout the game. They can be below deck (protected from enemy strikes), on deck arming for a strike, or in the air moving towards or away from a target. Fighters (F4F Wildcats or A6M Zero 'Zekes') can also be established in a combat air patrol (CAP) to protect their carrier.

The game ends when either sides carriers are all lost, or if one of the task forces leave the map.

200759.overview: In the game you are starting a session at the U.S. stock market with a beginning net worth equal to $10,000. Three companies from Computer, Oil & Gas, Retail Sales, Auto, and Heavy Industries are present on this market. Stock prices are changing each week due to economical, political, or social situations. On each turn you should examine the news and trends, and buy or sell a certain quantity of stocks in order to increase your net worth. Based on your net worth, you'll be classified by one of the five ranks: Novice, Investor, Speculator, Professional, or Broker. The higher rank you have, the more investment opportunities are available to you. The goal is to finish the session with as a high a net worth as possible; the highest rank is Millionaire. The game is available for single player and the game may be saved to be restored later.

200761.overview:
This real time all-text game puts you in the role of a Mind Adventurer, asked to journey back through the minds of four deceased residents of your planet in search of the Wheel of Wisdom. The Wheel is the only thing that can restore your planet from the state of chaos it's now in. The hardbound book that comes with the game includes the instructions and a novella-length introduction to the plot.

This game was the attempt by Synapse to compete with Infocom and their various adventures, and the underlying engine technology was actually internally known as "BTZ" (Better Than Zork). However only four of these style games were released.

200797.overview:
MicroSailing is a 1 - 2 player sailing game for the 8-bit Atari computer.

The player controls a small sailing vessel, which they must navigate past a number of pylons in the order demonstrated by a lead vessel. The player must then chart this course, while dealing with changing wind conditions. The first player to chart the correct course is the winner. Players can choose standard or advanced rules, as well as clear or stormy weather.

200848.overview:
Published in Compute! Magazine from issue 089 in October 1987. Act quickly—and don't panic—in this clever arcade-style game. In two weeks the Statewide Marbles Championship will be held in Louisville.. You've been practicing for nearly a year, and now, at the last minute, you find you've lost your favorite marble. You're going to have to collect every marble you can to find one as special as the one you lost.

"Marbles" is a hypnotic arcade style game in which you try to catch marbles in a bucket.

200929.overview: A standard platformer. After a jump is started (by pressing the stick up/left or right) the character can still be controlled by moving the stick left or right, and long jumps can be made by keeping the stick held up.

201042.overview:
The Midas Touch is a 1 - 2 player phrasal guessing game for the 8-but Atari computer

Two human players can compete, or the player competes against themselves. The player takes turns spinning a wheel that has numerous stones and other valuable material written it, and the value of the material corresponds to the score the player receives for each correct letter guessed. Vowels must be purchased. The first player to guess the entire phrase wins points for the round.

205555.overview:
Magneto is a game that's sort of a combination of Pong and Breakout. Pong because you don't have to break bricks like in breakout, but also Breakout because you play the game from a vertical perspective. Unlike Pong, however, there is no AI opponent. Rather you have to hit the ball off the top of the screen as often as you can without losing all your paddles.

The game was developed and released by Aim Software. The year of release is unknown as of right now, however.

211107.overview: Mystix II (also known as Mystix 2) is the sequel to Futurevision's German langauge graphic text adventure Mystix: World of Horror. It was released in 1992 (one year after the first game)

216886.overview: Variant of the Cluedo (or Clue for American readers) board game, you must solve a murder by moving around a mansion finding clues, interrogating suspects and finally proclaiming your accusation.

217651.overview: This budget game is essentially Kikstart without the engines. It's viewed from the side, with 12 courses to complete within their respective time limits. You control the bike by setting the speed and jumping at the right moments. Hazards to negotiate include hills, walls, rocks, spikes and ice. Some of these can be circumnavigated by buying the right add-ons from the shop after each race. The amount of money you have to spend is dependent upon how quickly you completed the previous race.

217902.overview: Matchbox Tic-Tac-Toe is a computerized version of Tic-Tac-Toe for the Atari 8-bits. It was developed by Joseph Hafner, and published as a type-in game in the April 1984 issue of Antic Magazine.

218020.overview:
Mission Shark is a platform game where a covert agent is trying to find four canisters within an enemy base. The goal of the game is to find them all and make it to the exit.

Moving around the game world, the agent must watch out for enemy soldiers, landmines, electric fields and defense turrets. Getting shot or touched by those hazards results in losing health, which can be replenished by collecting the appropriate power-up. The agent is armed with a gun and some grenades; ammo is limited, but more of it can be found.

218560.overview: A compilation of Paul Woakes's 3D exploration and flight game Mercenary, and the Second City expansion pack. Having crash-landed on the planet Targ, the player's main objective is to find a means of escape. There are several ways to achieve this end. A civil war between two factions affords the player an opportunity to earn money to buy their escape from Targ. Mercenary: The Second City, released in 1986, is an expansion pack. Initially its major distinction is the new color scheme, however, after a similar objective, the substantive differences reveal themselves subtly: there is a different city layout, a more intricate underground complex, a new set of puzzles to overcome and several significant changes with game objects.

220209.overview: Microchess 2.0 is a board game written by Peter Jennings and published by Personal Software in 1981 for the Atari.

418494.overview: The Object of the game is to destroy your opponent's castle by shooting through the blockade. The blockade must be hit 5 times in order to breakthrough.

418618.overview:
M-ss-ng L-nks is a 1 - 2 player educational game for multiple systems.

Players are given a short excerpt from a famous piece of literature with letters missing. The level of difficulty determines how many and how the letters are missing. The player's goal is to type in the missing letters. The player has 5 attempts per letter to complete each section, and if they fail, the letter is automatically filled. The player received a score of 100% if they fill in every letter correct the first try, with the score progressively decreasing from there.

418631.overview: MicroRhythm was part of a set of music creation software (then advertised as games) that used real sampled sounds and was essentially a drum-machine. It features three modes: 'BARS' mode was used to create individual patterns and 'SONG' mode to align patterns in desired order to create a tune (exactly as pattern-based music sequencers do). There was also a third Real-Time mode for playing with the keyboard. Simple flam effect and pitch adjust for every sample were also possible, as well as the main tempo change.

418636.overview:
Mar Tesoro (which is Spanish for Sea Treasure) is a game which simulates the search for sunken treasure. You start with $10,000 with which you must hire a boat, crew and equipment of various sorts from the main port of "The Island". Then you can explore and bring back any treasure that you find.

In port, you can hire a boat and select the type of equipment to use (scuba, diving rig or a diving bell). These allow you to reach treasure at increasing depths. You can also hire a historian who can estimate the worth of a treasure by a sample retrieved by the diver, without having to recover the entire treasure. Additional crew can be hired to assist in salvage operations. Once the daily hire charge and time has been determined, you can set out on your expedition.

On leaving port, you may choose to look at the chart which shows the randomly generated island, the surrounding sea, and previously dropped buoys. You can move the ship, represented by an asterisk, from square to square in four directions. Movement uses time, which is shown below the chart. If you exceed the agreed upon rental time you will be nabbed by the coast guard. Other randomly occurring incidents such as bad weather and engine trouble may also use time.

Once you have decided upon a spot to search, you may dive. This brings up a side view of the scene. You control the diver, who must visit the ocean floor and return a sample of any possible treasure. Treasure, which ranges from a shipwreck to an oyster bed with pearls, usually appears a different colour from the rest of the sea floor. It may also be guarded by a giant squid, which must be avoided, or you will lose a worker or perhaps your own life. Having brought the sample back to the boat, you have the option of retrieving the treasure. The historian (if you have one) will offer an opinion on the likelihood of a good treasure. The time it takes to retrieve a treasure depends on the depth. If you don't have enough time, you can mark the site with a buoy and continue elsewhere.

After returning to port, you are offered money for all of your recovered treasures. Then you may either leave the game (and get you final rating), or continue the game to look for even greater fortune.

418647.overview: This updated version by David N. Plotkin, was originally released on the Atari 2600.

418650.overview:
Mix & Match is a 1-player memory game for the 8-bit Atari.

Four colored squares displayed on the screen beep in sequence, and the player must repeat back the sequence. The sequence prolongs by 1 each time, and the goal is to memorize as long of sequence as possible without making a mistake.

418663.overview: Monkey up a Tree is a simple educational game for kids teaching mathematical operations for up to two players. By giving the right answers the player must lead the monkey to the top of the tree, where the award is waiting - a fresh banana. The game contains all the four basic mathematical operations: addition, subtraction, division, multiplication.

418681.overview:
Moptown Hotel is an educational logic game for multiple systems.

An early educational game that teaches logic and pattern recognition skills for ages 9 and up. It uses a set of creatures called Moppets, which can be Gribbits (with tails) or Bibbits (with large feet), fat or thin, tall or short, and red or blue. Consists of a number of mini-games:

Who's Next Door? - The player has 3 characters, where one change has been made from the top row to the bottom row. The player must guess the correct missing character in the bottom row.

Change Me - The player must move between the character on the left and the character on the right by making 1 or 2 attribute changes in each pane.

Spot Me - The player is presented with 4 Moppets, and must determine which one has a trait that is different than the other 3, and what that trait is.

Happy Birthday? - The player needs to choose which Moppet has their birthday today. All 16 Moppet combinations appear, and the player must choose one. For each choice, the player is told one characteristic which is incorrect, until they can narrow down the correct Moppet.

Secret Pal - Similar to the board game Master Mind, the player must attempt to guess the characteristics of a Moppet, and each guess are told how many of 4 attributes are correct.

Moptown Map The player has a 4 x 4 square, that Moppets must be filled in. Each row and column has two rules for who can live there. The game tells the player which Moppets are placed correctly.

Moptown Hotel - The player attempts to place Moppets in a 4 x 4 grid, where they must have only 1 or 2 characteristics different than all surrounding Moppets. The player receives a bonus based upon number of Moppets placed.

418684.overview:
Mugwump is a 1-player strategy game for the 8-bit Atari computer.

You've been mugwump hunting all weekend. It's damp and cold in this swamp, but at last you have four of the critters cornered. They are hiding in a 10 x 10 swamp, and each turn you search one location in the swamp, and are informed the distance you are from all 4 creatures. Using this information, you must try to catch all the mugwumps in 10 turns or less.

418687.overview: One of the oldest releases by The Learning Company, Moptown Parade is an edutainment game aimed at teaching basic pattern recognition and logic skills to kids aged 4-7. The goal is simple: choose the traits of Moppet creatures to line up in a queue, obeying the given number of rules. For instance, if the rule says "2," you must choose the traits of the next Moppet so that it differs from the previous Moppet by 2 traits, e.g. a fat, blue Moppet can stand next to a thin, red Moppet. The number of rules, i.e. traits, can be changed from 1 to 4, thus either making the game more or less challenging (although changing the traits to 4, the maximum, will just result in your Moppets being an alternate sequence of two types of Moppets).

418784.overview: Move a marble through complex mazes avoiding damaging anything.

418919.overview:
Monday Morning Manager is a baseball management game that continues the tradition of the primarily text-based predecessors like SSI's Computer Baseball and Computer Statis Pro Baseball.

It includes 64 major league teams from 1905 through the 1985 playoff teams, with 1,500 players and pitchers in total. Most of the game is text based, but there is also a graphical display of the matches.

Players can create custom teams or manage existing ones. It is also possible to print rosters, box scores and league leaders.

418922.overview:
Match Up! is a 1-player educational game for multiple systems.

There are 3 modes of gameplay:* Matching Game: Matching a pair of the same family within 2, 4, or 8 objects.

Not Game: Choose which item does not look-alike, or is not in the same family.
Sorting Game: Divide items into "Look-Alikes" and "Families". Objects must be placed in 3 separate columns depending on which group they belong.

418975.overview:
The Mouse that Ate Chicago is the fifteenth in series of monthly text adventures for multiple systems.

The greedy and warped mind of Professor Rainier Frankenfeld has led to the creation if an enlarging ray, which can make any object several hundred times its normal size. As the professor prepares to enlarge a diamond, several mice scamper into the field. Four mice, Sam, Maja, Puji, and Fiji have been enlarged to gigantic size, and begin to wreck havoc about Chicago. The player, while out joyriding in their truck in the outskirts of Chicago, runs out of fuel. It is around that time, that they start to notice the surrounding mouse-related devastation. The player must use trickery to defeat the four mice to protect the inhabitants of Chicago.

All commands are via 2-word VERB NOUN entries, and game play contains several object puzzles. There is no save and restore feature.

418976.overview:
Menagerie Adventure is the sixteenth in a series of monthly text adventures for multiple systems.

While out on a pasture, you see strange vehicle ahead that appears to be a spaceship. As you are drawn closer, the door opens and you walk inside. Stepping inside, the door suddenly closes, and the alien vessel rapidly accelerates into space. You realize you've been captured aboard an alien zoo ship, and you are to be their newest attraction. Captured aboard the alien vessel, the player must explore the ship, and use the assistance of other alien creatures from throughout the solar system to escape your prison. Each of these creatures from different planets have unique skills which will allow the player to finally access the navigation control of the alien vessel, and reroute the vessel back to Earth, allowing their escape.

All commands are via 2-word VERB NOUN entries, and game play contains several object puzzles. There is no save and restore feature.

419040.overview:
Maxwell's Demon and Memory Mania is a re-release of Bishop's Square and Maxwell's Demon originally published by  Datasoft Inc. The release includes two games:-

Memory Mania is a tile-sliding puzzle game. A picture is split into a number of separate tiles, from 4 - 64, and randomly shuffled. The player must restore the individual photo by sliding the rows and columns of tile pieces. Initially came with 3 photos: deer, cube, and desert. The game tracks the number of moves made to solve a puzzle, and the player can save a puzzle in progress.

Maxwell's Demon is based upon the second law of thermodynamics, but in this case the goal is to prove it wrong. The player controls James Clerk Maxwell's imaginary demon which sits upon the gate of separation between two molecules, by attempting to separate a system of fast moving hydrogen and slow moving helium atoms by opening and closing a gate that separates two chambers. The gate can be moved vertically, and can be briefly opened to allow molecules through. The goal is to separate all the atoms in the system.

419065.overview:
Midway is a 1 player versus computer variant of the board game Battleship.

Played on a 17 x 8 grid, each player places 10 ships, and each ship only takes up one space. Ships have different point values, and each player starts with 1 carrier, 1 tanker, 2 battleships, 3 destroyers, and 3 submarines. Each player takes a turn typing in a coordinate to see if they hit and destroy the enemy vessel. Previously played squares are shown on the board. Players get to decide how many turns the game will last, and the player with the highest score at the end is the victor.

419093.overview:
Midway Battles is a strategy wargame for the 8-bit Atari.

It is June 4th, 1942. You stand on the bridge of the carrier Enterprise observing your attack planes warming up on the deck, exhaust flames belching in the dawn light of this fateful day. The search planes have been out since early morning, looking for the fleet that was sighted by Midway planes yesterday. You feel terribly outclassed, seeking to engage the undefeated Imperial Japanese navy with your meager forces.

The player can participate with human or computer opponent. The Historical Midway Scenario, No Coral Sea Operation, and Random Encounter Scenario are available. The player can choose to add carriers, battleships, or both to either the American or Japanese forces. The player assigns their ships to a number of task forces. Each turn the player and Japanese forces move their ships on an overview screen, and can review the condition of their forces. The player can send out searches from Midway or their task forces, and can attack or send out a combat air patrol if enemy ships are detected.

419224.overview:
Market Forces is a 1 - 8 player commodities trading simulation.

When you play Market Forces, you can experience the actual effects of a market economy without risking your shirt. At the beginning of each turn, players are supplied a market analysis, and which commodities might be hot in the future. Players take turns buying and selling 5 separate commodities: corn, bacon, coffee, orange juice, and sugar. The player selects the amount of commodity they wish to purchase and how much they are willing to play, but this information is not conveyed to their competitors.

The amount of commodity the player actually receives depends upon the number of purchases by their competitors, and the price that they are paying. If the competitor is willing to pay more, then they will get the entirety of the resource. If the player purchases more than they can afford, they will rack up debt, and if they can not pay this off, they will declare bankruptcy and lose. Next comes the selling phase, where players offload the goods they purchased. Any goods not sold will be lost, as they can not be stored for a year. The number of units sold once again depends on the player's selling price and that of their competitors, and there is risk the player may not be able to offload their goods if they ask for too much.

Gameplay takes place over 6 turns, with the player who has the most money at the end is declared the winner.

420098.overview:
Compilation of 4 puzzle games:- 

Mind Buster - Match the original pattern as quick as you can without losing your mind. 

Zone X - Find the X on the color grid. 

Towers - A challenging game to move the tower pieces across the screen. 

Code Breaker - Break the code before it breaks you.

420113.overview:
Mountain Shoot is a 2-player artillery game.

Two pieces of artillery line up on hilly terrain, and take turns firing at each other. The first player to hit the other wins. Each turn the player types the direction of their shot and how much powder they wish to use. Allows for 3 levels of difficulty, and the option for limited powder. Wind direction and strength is randomized each turn, and terrain is randomized each game. The program keeps track of score over multiple games.

420117.overview: From the depths of the sea emerged the island of evil, and horror descended upon Vandor. the lovely planet - famous for its wines, its festivals. The sun lost its light to the evil that now rules Vandor. Villages and towns are deserted, the once enticing forests are dangerous. Barren the valleys, forbidding the mountains, on whose slopes wine once fermented. When the night plunges the planet Vandor into black, one gathers in the stronghold and listens to the stories about the one who will set Vandor free again. So proclaimed Shandra the magician. But who dares to face the forces of darkness? Who is strong enough, clever and wise enough to interpret the few clues? Who dares enter the ice caves of Modra to find the king who left the land of Kruzia in grief and holds the key that could change everything? Shandra the magician foresaw all of this. Nobody listened to him. - But Shandra is also the only one who still believes in rescue. No treasures beckon to the capable, the one longed for, no other reward than to bring Vandor back to freedom and to know: Evil can be conquered! Are you strong enough, friend? Then face the myth!

421451.overview: The Mad Marble Maze was published as a type-in game and is based on the arcade hit Marble Madness. Your task is to steer a ball through the maze to the goal within a time limit.

457831.overview:
MiG Alley Ace is an action-based simulation of air combat during the Korean War. The titular MiG Alley was the area over North Korea near the Chinese border where the world's first large-scale jet-to-jet air battles took place, with, among others, the American F-86 Sabre facing off against the Soviet MiG-15 Fagot.

The game is similar to MicroProse's earlier simulations Hellcat Ace and Spitfire Ace. MiG Alley Ace differs in that it offers a two-player mode via split screen. Five different scenarios based on actual encounters from the war are available. Each can be played solo, cooperatively or head-to-head. The goal in each scenario is to shoot down as many of the enemy planes as possible before the own squadron is destroyed. If a player's plane is destroyed but other craft from their squadron remain, they take control over one of the surviving planes. A scenario can result in a victory or loss for either side (or a neutral result in case the time limit expires). What the result is depends on a number of factors - while a destroyed enemy plane always nets victory points, the enemy might not be punished for it if the pilot bailed out or ditched the plane. Losing a scenario deducts from the player's lives: too many losses means the game has to be restarted.

461098.overview:
Masterblazer is a two-player-only sports game set in a futuristic competition where players control vehicles competing in an isometric playfield where the players maneuver vehicles in competitive matches resembling futuristic ball games. 
 
From volume 4, issue 5 of Computronic dated September / October 1987.
